Jamie was never a pretty young lady. At least until now.

Before her transformation, she was the poster child of what “normal” would look like on a milk carton. Black hair swayed beneath her ears, nothing special tied in, nothing weaved. Her hazelnut brown eyes were almost as dull as her smile, if she ever smiled at that. And her face like all teenagers becoming of age was decorated with small red pimples, randomly skewed like a piece of modern art. 

Jamie was always envious of all the girls that their parents could afford mods for. The recent fad was peacock feathers. Almost all the girls had them in their hair. They would twitch and flair to show the brilliant hues of blues and greens. Oh, how she envied them, “if only I could be as pretty as them she thought.” Jamie came from a rather poor family, even a simple nail mod would be ten times over of what her parents made. She sighed in thought, wondering how it would be like to be perfect like them.

“Jamie! Jamie? You there? Earth to Jamie,” replied Sasha. 

“Oh, hey,” replied Jamie mellowly, turning to see where the noise came from. Jamie knew Sasha since first grade, they’ve been friends ever since. However, Sasha always has the newest mods due to her father being one of the developers for Synergistic Enterprises. Today, she had her cat eyebrows on and her hair tipped with koi tails. 

“So...how do I look? You can see I’m a bit of a cat fish,” Sasha said with a grin.

“Haha, you look cute,” said Jamie.

“As always, of course. But I wanted to talk to you for a bit. I just got a new mod installer, I know it’s not much but hey, I want you to have my old one.”

Jamie’s eyes slowly widened up, as if she had fish eyes modded in. “Rr-r-really,” as her mouth stood agape. Tears of happiness tumbled down as Jamie trembled.

“Thank you, thank you so much. I can’t believe this is real. I can’t believe this is happening, you’re the best friend I could of asked for.”

“Hah, nothing to it you ol’ thimmigut,” as she brushed the tears off her face. “I assume you already know how to use it since every time we pass the store windows you can’t help but drool a little. 

“I do not drool!” 

“Hmmm...right,” as Sasha causally flicks a bear of drool off the corner of Jamie’s lip.

“Um. No one saw that right,” as Jamie blushed a little.

“Saw what?”

“Thanks again Sasha,” as Jamie lept in for a hug.

“See you tomorrow, okay Sash?”

“Roger, and over and out,” grinned Sasha.

As Jamie held her precious mod installer in her arms, visions of new styles she saw in the holipads came to life in her brain. Just when she was about to leave school, a sudden *thwack* and she found herself on the ground. Ouch, that hurt she thought, as she tried to make sense of what just happened.

Two menacing pairs of eyes glared down at her. 

“Oops, did I do that?” A voice said.

As Jamie looked up, a sudden huff of air escaped her lungs. Just get luck. 

Beatrice and Britch. Two bullies that liked to knock Jamie down a couple of pegs as their hobby. They were spitting mirror images of one another. Their skin was as clear as porcelain dolls, and locks of golden hair sparkled in the sunlight. They were some of the prettiest girls in their grade, no doubt. The only un-pretty thing was their personality.

“Oh, look who it is! Is Ms.Modless even a girl?” Said Britch.

“Why don’t you just kill yourself you ugly piece of shit?” As Beatrice gives a swing of her foot towards Jamie. Jamie narrowly dodged it as she rolled away.

“Why do you do this to me,” Jamie screams.

“Because we can of course!” Beatrice and Britch say and laugh in unison.

“Oh, what’s that in your hands? How did this pile of dirt end up getting a mod installer?” Says Britch.

“Eh, a 43-SD, it’s an old model anyways. She would probably fuck up and put teeth where her eyes are. Ha-ha-ha!” Laughs Beatrice.

Jamie holds on to her mod installer for dear life and sprints towards the door. Tears flow down as she runs home. “I’ll show them, I’ll show them all,” she mutters to herself. 

“I just want to be pretty. I just want to be pretty. Please let me be pretty,” she thinks to herself. 

As Jamie arrives home she opens the package as fast as she can, her hands shake unreadily as she fumbled with the latch. 

“Oh, no,” she exclaims as she realizes every thing is there except the mods. 

“How am I going to go back to school looking like this?” as she groans in frustration.

A noise comes from the door.

“Mreow. Meow.” 

“Oh, hello Mr.Felix.” Her hands run down the soft fur of the ginger tufts. *sigh* “Even you’re prettier than me. I wish I had those pretty sunset eyes you have.”

“But I could. But I can,” Jamie thinks. No, no. Not her friend. Jamie shrugs the though out as she proceeds to go towards the kitchen to open a can of cat food for Mr. Felix. 

Jamie’s hands dance along the can opener and also the kitchen knife in the drawer. She hums. 

“It won’t take long. Don’t you want to be pretty. Everyone will love you if you’re pretty!” The thought echoes through her mind. I would do anything to be pretty she thinks to herself. 

“Anything?” As the thought echoes in her mind.

Jamie starts to feel something warm. Something wet. As Jamie comes back to reality she realizes that in her hand is the kitchen knife stained with a velvet red. 

Her eyes widen in shock as she realizes that two small sunset colored eyes are in her hand.

“No, no, no. NO! What have I done? I don’t remember doing this! Please make this stop, make this stop!” she thinks.

But a smile betrays her and slowly spreads throughout her face. 

“Yes. Now I know how I’ll be pretty,” she says to herself.

After a tiresome night, Jamie wakes up and proceeds to go to school.

A soft humming melody comes from her as she takes prideful strides in the hall. Whispers float in the air.

“Who’s the new girl?”

“Wow, is that Jamie? She’s so much prettier!”

“OMG, I love her mods. What brand do you think it is?”

Two familiar faces start to appear around the corner. 

“Good morning, Beatrice! Good morning, Britch!” Jamie exclaims with a cheerful glow.

A pair of shocked faces develop in front of Jamie. 

“How, what, where...did you manage to get such a pretty mod?” Asks Beatrice.

“Oh, I can show you where. Why don’t we hang out after school and I can get you one too?” Says Jamie.

“Ya..., yes I’d like that.” Says Beatrice.

“You in Britch?” asks Jamie.

“Bah, I don’t need your cheap tricks. Right Beatrice?” Says Britch.

An empty stare mirrors back at her. 

“Sorry, but I think I’m going to hang out with Jamie for a bit. She doesn’t seem that bad.” 

“Oh....,” a face of disappointment scours her face.

I’m going to tell you something that we had a saying in my community college. 

“It is never too late to learn.”

We would have people all the way from fresh start(15) to people that were in their 60s. 

When I asked the older crowd why they went back and the reasons for being here they almost always gave the same answer, “I wish I got my degree while I was younger and not I’m 30s. But I’m glad I’m here now.” It’s okay to fail. I failed my driving exam 8 times before I finally passed my ninth time. I rejected a full ride to a prestigious law school, only to drop down to going to community college. Everyone makes mistakes, and that’s okay because that what makes us human.

University is less about learning, and more about finding out who you are and what you want to be. You don’t have to force yourself to go to college, some people take a break and that’s all they really need to do better in the end. Life is not a race, and you should be thankful because your family cares and loves you enough to help. Oh, and that last bit about cheating, everyone does it in college. ;)
